record.original_question: Which square-free words are themselves shuffles of square-free words?

evidence.quote: Which square-free words w are themselves shuﬄes of square-free words: w = u  u?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and A* the free monoid of finite words over A. A word w ∈ A* is square-free if it contains no nonempty factor of the form xx (i.e., there are no nonempty u and words p,s with w = p·uu·s). Given two words u,v ∈ A*, the shuffle set u ⧢ v ⊆ A* consists of all words obtained by interleaving u and v while preserving the relative order of letters within each. A shuffled-square is a word w that lies in u ⧢ u for some nonempty word u.

Characterize the set of square-free words w (over any alphabet) such that w is a shuffled-square, i.e., such that there exists a square-free word u with w ∈ u ⧢ u. In particular, give a structural description (or decision procedure) for finite square-free words w admitting a square-free word u with w ∈ u ⧢ u, and determine for which alphabet sizes there exist infinite square-free words w that arise as a shuffle u ⧢ u of an infinite square-free word u with itself.
artifact.status_search_result: The general characterization question appears to remain open. Existence results are known: Harju and Müller showed that for every n ≥ 3 there is a square-free ternary word u of length n with u ⧢ u containing a square-free word, and that there is an infinite square-free word u over three letters whose self-shuffle yields an infinite square-free word. Related questions on shuffled-square-free words (avoiding any factor in u ⧢ u) have been studied by Currie, Müller, Guégan–Ochem, and others, with progress on alphabet size, but no complete structural characterization of square-free words that are self-shuffles of square-free words has been published.

status_evidence.snippet: Studies words avoiding shuffled squares; alphabet-size questions remain open.
